children: SoftBank Group (SOBKY), the Japanese technology-investment and artificial-intelligence powerhouse, tumbled roughly 5.1% to $15.335 Wednesday as investors sized up SB Energy's planned U.S. IPO. The headline number is breathtaking: approximately $439 billion in contracted backlog. The reality check is just as dramatic. SB Energy does not have a single operational data center.

The financial gap is enormous. First-half revenue surged 66.4% to $138.7 million, but the net loss ballooned from $215.5 million to $3.21 billion. Nvidia has committed $1.5 billion at the IPO price, while OpenAI holds warrants valued at nearly $5.5 billion. SoftBank's announcement confirms that the registration statement is public, but the share count and pricing are still missing. Investors know an IPO is coming. They still do not know the price of admission.

Now comes the hard part. That staggering backlog equals more than 3,100 times first-half revenue, yet it spans long-term contractsnot cash arriving tomorrow. OpenAI and SoftBank are also expected to generate a hefty slice of early lease revenue, raising concentration and related-party concerns. The valuation snapshot adds pressure: SoftBank's $15.335 share price sits 7.77% above its GF Value estimate of $14.23. The IPO could unlock billions for SoftBank, but SB Energy must turn AI ambition into working data centers, paying customers and real cash flow.

title: SoftBank's $439 Billion AI Backlog Arrives With a $3.21 Billion Loss
